overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed executive session minutes for the 3:00 p.m. May 12, 2015 session and the May 15 and May 20, 2015 sessions; no intentional violation was found, and the Board was ordered to comply, amend and release the minutes, and certify. The conclusion says "May 15 and 18," but the discussion addresses May 20, a discrepancy the letter does not resolve.

allegations.summary: Jan 24, 2011 executive session minutes allegedly omitted the executive session start time.
allegations.key_passage: We have not construed the Open Meeting Law as requiring meeting minutes to separately list the start time of an executive session nor the start time for particular discussion topics.

allegations.summary: Jan 24, 2011 executive session minutes allegedly failed to list documents or exhibits used.
allegations.key_passage: we find no indication that the Board used any documents or exhibits during the executive session, and therefore the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to include such a list.

allegations.summary: Jan 24, 2011 executive session summary allegedly too brief and insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find that the minutes include an insufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that took place.

allegations.summary: May 12, 2015 (3:00 p.m.) executive session minutes allegedly failed to list documents or exhibits used.
allegations.key_passage: there is no indication that any documents or exhibits were used during this executive session.

allegations.summary: May 12, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly omitted the full name of the police lieutenant discussed.
allegations.key_passage: the minutes clearly include a first and last name of the individual who was discussed

allegations.summary: May 12, 2015 (3:00 p.m.) executive session minutes allegedly gave an insufficient summary; the minutes only said a discussion occurred.
allegations.key_passage: we find the minutes insufficient where they merely state that a discussion took place without summarizing the discussion that occurred.

allegations.summary: May 12, 2015 (3:30 p.m.) executive session minutes allegedly gave an insufficient summary of a brief session with no discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Where the minutes clearly document that no discussion took place during a meeting lasting less than two minutes, and the Board merely voted to continue the meeting to a specified future date and time, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: May 15, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly gave an insufficient summary of contract negotiations.
allegations.key_passage: For a meeting lasting approximately 15 minutes, we find the minutes insufficient where they merely state that contract discussions took place without including any summary of the discussions or negotiations that took place, such as an identification of the issues being negotiated or the proposals from the parties.

allegations.summary: May 15, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly failed to list documents or exhibits used in contract negotiations.
allegations.key_passage: We are unable to conclude that any particular document—such as a prior contract or draft contract—was used in the course of the negotiations

allegations.summary: May 15, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly omitted the full name of the police lieutenant discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we have not construed the Open Meeting Law as requiring meeting minutes to include first and last names, especially where, as here, the minutes identify the individuals in question using identifying titles

allegations.summary: May 20, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly gave an insufficient summary of contract negotiations.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons we find the May 15, 2015, executive session meeting minutes insufficient, we also find the summary of the discussions in the May 20, 2015, meeting minutes insufficient.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's minute violations were intentional; the Board insisted its minutes complied with the law.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find no evidence that the Board intentionally violated the Law or acted with deliberate ignorance of the Law’s requirements.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent.

Amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes for the May 12 (3:00 p.m.), May 15 and May 18, 2015 meetings, and release them to the public, except portions lawfully withheld under G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
Certify to the AG's office within 45 days of receipt of the letter that it has complied with the order.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Board to amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes for the meetings held at 3:00 p.m. on May 12, 2015, and on May 15 and 18, 2015, and to release those minutes to the public, unless any portion thereof may lawfully be withheld in accordance with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
